question: Under KRS 324.010(4), which of the following best defines a Kentucky "principal broker"?
choice_a: A broker licensed under KRS 324.046 who, in addition to performing acts of real estate brokerage, is the single broker responsible for the operation of the company with which he or she is associated
choice_b: Any broker who owns a majority of a real estate brokerage's stock
choice_c: A broker who has held an active license for at least ten consecutive years
choice_d: The broker in an office who lists the most properties in a calendar year
explanation: KRS 324.010(4) defines a "principal broker" as a person licensed as a broker under KRS 324.046 who, in addition to performing acts of real estate brokerage, is the single broker responsible for the operation of the company with which he or she is associated.

question: A Kentucky real estate brokerage is organized as an LLC. Which statement correctly describes how KREC licensing works for that business?
choice_a: The LLC itself must obtain a separate KREC company license in addition to its principal broker's individual license
choice_b: KRS Chapter 324 does not issue a separate company/entity license; instead, the company operates under a principal broker who is personally the single broker responsible for the company's operation
choice_c: Only the LLC's majority member needs to hold any real estate license
choice_d: LLCs are barred from engaging in real estate brokerage in Kentucky
explanation: Kentucky licenses individuals (brokers and sales associates), not the business entity itself. KRS 324.010(4) makes the principal broker "the single broker responsible for the operation of the company," and KRS 324.040(2) requires each applicant to state the name of the person or company with which he or she will be associated -- there is no separate corporate/company licensing statute in KRS Chapter 324.

question: Under KRS 324.112(1), a principal broker may maintain a branch office outside what radius of the main office only if a broker is managing that branch office?
choice_a: 25 miles
choice_b: 50 miles
choice_c: 100 miles
choice_d: 150 miles
explanation: KRS 324.112(1) provides that no principal broker shall maintain a branch office outside a one hundred (100) mile radius of the main office without having a broker managing the branch office.

question: Within a 100-mile radius of the main office, who is permitted to manage a branch office besides a broker, under KRS 324.112(2)?
choice_a: Any licensed sales associate, regardless of experience
choice_b: An unlicensed office administrator designated by the principal broker
choice_c: Only a sales associate who has completed the 21-hour broker prelicensing course
choice_d: A sales associate with two years' experience in real estate, averaging at least 20 hours per week for 24 months prior
explanation: KRS 324.112(2) allows a sales associate with two (2) years' experience in the real estate business, averaging at least twenty (20) hours per week for a period of twenty-four (24) months prior, to manage a branch office inside a one hundred (100) mile radius of the main office.

question: Under KRS 324.112(3), within how many days of creating a branch office must the principal broker register it with the Kentucky Real Estate Commission?
choice_a: 10 days
choice_b: 5 days
choice_c: 15 days
choice_d: 30 days
explanation: KRS 324.112(3) requires the principal broker to register any branch office with the commission within ten (10) days of the creation of the branch office.

question: Per KRS 324.112(4), where must a licensee's license be kept on file?
choice_a: At the licensee's personal residence
choice_b: In the office in which the licensee is actively engaged and affiliated
choice_c: Permanently at the Commission's Frankfort office
choice_d: With the licensee's errors-and-omissions insurance carrier
explanation: KRS 324.112(4) states that the licenses of all licensees shall be kept on file in the office in which they are actively engaged and affiliated.

question: Under KRS 324.112(5), a principal broker who is closing his or her real estate brokerage business may temporarily affiliate with another principal broker only if certain conditions are met. Which of the following is one of those required conditions?
choice_a: The closing broker posts a $500 closure bond with the Commission
choice_b: Notice of the closure is published in a local newspaper for two consecutive weeks
choice_c: No other licensee is affiliated with the former principal broker, and both brokers give the Commission satisfactory assurances that no consumer will be adversely affected by the affiliation or closing
choice_d: The two brokerage firms must permanently merge into a single entity
explanation: KRS 324.112(5) permits temporary affiliation for closing a business only if no other licensee is affiliated with the former principal broker, both brokers represent to the commission that the affiliation is for closing the business, and both give assurances satisfactory to the commission that no consumer will be adversely affected.

question: Under KRS 324.115(1), every broker licensed under KRS 324.045 is generally required to do what?
choice_a: Personally own the real property where the brokerage office is located
choice_b: Employ at least two sales associates at all times
choice_c: Lease office space of at least 500 square feet
choice_d: Maintain a definite place of business in Kentucky
explanation: KRS 324.115(1) requires that, except as provided for certain nonresident brokers, every broker licensed under KRS 324.045 shall maintain a definite place of business in this state.

question: Under KRS 324.115(2), a nonresident Kentucky broker is excused from maintaining an active place of business in Kentucky only if which set of conditions is satisfied?
choice_a: The broker maintains a business place in the state of original licensure, that state's reciprocity agreement with the Commission does not require Kentucky licensees to maintain an office there, and this does not conflict with the Commission's reciprocity agreement with that state
choice_b: The broker simply requests a waiver in writing, with no further conditions
choice_c: The broker has fewer than five active Kentucky listings
choice_d: The broker is a member of the National Association of Realtors
explanation: KRS 324.115(2) sets out three conjunctive conditions: maintaining a business place in the state of original licensure, that state's reciprocity agreement not requiring Kentucky licensees to maintain an office there, and no conflict with the Commission's reciprocity agreement.

question: Under KRS 324.230, what happens to the licenses of sales associates affiliated with a principal broker whose license is revoked or suspended?
choice_a: They are automatically and permanently canceled
choice_b: They are automatically rendered inactive pending a change of principal broker and issuance of a new license
choice_c: They remain fully active regardless of the principal broker's status
choice_d: Each associate must immediately retake and pass the licensing examination
explanation: KRS 324.230 provides that revocation or suspension of a principal broker's license automatically renders inactive every license granted to any person by virtue of association with that broker, pending a change of principal broker and issuance of a new license (issued without charge if granted in the same year as the original).

question: Under KRS 324.425, if a principal broker dies or becomes otherwise incapacitated, the Commission may, in its discretion, permit a sales associate to complete and close the broker's existing business for a temporary period not to exceed:
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 90 days
choice_c: 6 months
choice_d: 1 year
explanation: KRS 324.425 allows the commission, in its discretion based on the merits of the case, to permit one of the sales associates to complete and close the existing business of a deceased or incapacitated principal broker for a temporary period not to exceed six (6) months.

question: Except for the limited circumstances authorized under KRS 324.112(1) and 324.425, what does KRS 324.020(5) provide regarding sales associates?
choice_a: A sales associate may supervise another licensed sales associate after five years in the business
choice_b: Any sales associate may manage an office with the written consent of clients
choice_c: Supervisory authority may be delegated by majority vote of the office's associates
choice_d: No sales associate shall supervise another licensed sales associate or manage a real estate brokerage office
explanation: KRS 324.020(5) states that, except as authorized in KRS 324.112(1) and 324.425, no sales associate shall supervise another licensed sales associate or manage a real estate brokerage office.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the requirements a licensee must meet under KRS 324.310(2) to place a license in inactive status?
choice_a: The licensee must first complete 48 hours of post-license education
choice_b: The licensee must not engage in any real estate activity for others during the inactive term
choice_c: The licensee must pay the biennial license renewal fees for each biennial period the license is inactive
choice_d: The licensee must obtain extended reporting period coverage insurance for one year at the then-current minimum requirements prior to entering inactive status
explanation: KRS 324.310(2) conditions inactive status on not engaging in real estate activity for others, paying biennial renewal fees during inactivity, and obtaining one year of extended reporting period insurance coverage. Post-license education (48 hours) is a separate requirement tied to initial sales associate licensure, not to placing a license in inactive status.

question: Under KRS 324.310(4), which of the following is required to reactivate a license placed in inactive status?
choice_a: Retaking and passing the full original licensing examination in every case
choice_b: Submitting an acceptable criminal record check, completing all required continuing education, and paying the applicable reactivation fees
choice_c: Obtaining a new sponsoring principal broker with at least ten years of experience
choice_d: Waiting a mandatory 18-month cooling-off period before applying
explanation: KRS 324.310(4) requires a licensee reactivating from inactive status to submit an acceptable criminal record check consistent with KRS 324.045(4), complete all continuing education requirements, and pay the applicable reactivation fees. A new exam is not generally required for reactivation from inactive status (KRS 324.045(2) reserves the exam requirement for revoked, suspended, or long-expired licenses).

question: Under KRS 324.287(5), the reactivation fee the Commission may charge a licensee reactivating a license shall not exceed:
explanation: KRS 324.287(5) caps the reactivation fee at not more than ten dollars ($10).

question: Per KRS 324.010(16), a Kentucky license is placed in "canceled" status when a licensee fails to renew, fails to re-affiliate with a principal broker, writes a bad check for fees, or fails to complete continuing/post-license education. Per KRS 324.160(2), such a canceled license may be renewed, without a new exam, if the licensee pays all fees and meets active licensure requirements within:
choice_a: 90 days of cancellation
choice_b: 6 months of cancellation
choice_c: 2 years of the cancellation date
choice_d: 1 year of the cancellation date
explanation: KRS 324.160(2) provides that a canceled license may be renewed if the licensee pays all necessary fees and meets all other active licensure requirements within one (1) year of the cancellation date; no brokerage activity or compensation is permitted during the cancellation period (except compensation earned before cancellation).

question: Under KRS 324.090(3), a license not renewed by the end of the biennial license period automatically reverts to "expired" status. Such an expired license may be reactivated, upon payment of delinquent fees, before a lapse of:
choice_a: 1 year
choice_b: 6 months
choice_c: 2 years
choice_d: 5 years
explanation: KRS 324.090(3) states that any license not renewed at the end of the biennial license period automatically reverts to expired status, and an expired license may be reactivated before a lapse of one (1) year if delinquent fees are paid.

question: Which of the following changes does KRS 324.330(1) NOT, by itself, require a licensee to notify the Commission of in writing?
choice_a: A change of principal business location
choice_b: A licensee taking a two-week personal vacation
choice_c: A change of firm name
choice_d: A sales associate's transfer from one principal broker to another
explanation: KRS 324.330(1) requires written notice to the commission of any change of principal business location, change of firm name, a sales associate's transfer from one principal broker to another, or a change of surname; the commission then issues a new license for the unexpired period and charges the applicable fee. A personal vacation triggers no such notice requirement.

question: Under KRS 324.287(4)(a), the fee the Commission may charge for a licensee's transfer from one principal broker to another shall not exceed:
explanation: KRS 324.287(4)(a) caps the standard fee for a transfer from one principal broker to another at not more than ten dollars ($10) -- not twenty-five dollars, a figure that does not appear in the current statute.

question: Under KRS 324.287(4)(b), if a principal broker initiates a bulk transfer for 20 or more licensees at once, the transfer fee the Commission may charge shall not exceed:
explanation: KRS 324.287(4)(b) provides that if the transfer is initiated by the principal broker for twenty (20) or more licensees, the transfer fee shall not exceed two hundred dollars ($200).

question: Under KRS 324.330(2), a licensee must notify the Commission in writing of a change of residence address within how many days?
choice_a: 10 days
choice_b: 5 days
choice_c: 20 days
choice_d: 30 days
explanation: KRS 324.330(2) requires the commission to be notified in writing of a change of residence address within ten (10) days.

question: Per KRS 324.287(6), the fee for certification of a licensee's status with the Commission is:
explanation: KRS 324.287(6) sets the certification-of-status fee at ten dollars ($10).

question: Under KRS 324.160(6), when may a principal broker be held primarily liable for an affiliated licensee's unlawful act or violation of KRS Chapter 324?
choice_a: Whenever any affiliated licensee violates the chapter, regardless of the broker's knowledge
choice_b: Only if the violation occurred at the main office rather than a branch office
choice_c: Only if the broker had knowledge of the unlawful violation and did not prevent it
choice_d: Only if the broker personally received a commission on the transaction
explanation: KRS 324.160(6) provides that no unlawful act or violation by an affiliated licensee shall be cause for holding the principal broker primarily liable, unless the broker has knowledge of the unlawful violation and did not prevent it.

question: Under KRS 324.160(6), what supervisory duty is imposed on the principal broker (and designated manager, if any), and what is the consequence of failing to meet it?
choice_a: They must personally co-sign every purchase contract before it is binding
choice_b: They must carry a minimum $1 million supervisory bond
choice_c: They must review every associate's marketing materials weekly, with no statutory consequence for failing to do so
choice_d: They must exercise adequate supervision over the activities of licensed affiliates and all company employees to ensure violations do not occur; failure to do so is itself a violation of the chapter
explanation: KRS 324.160(6) requires the principal broker and designated manager, if any, to exercise adequate supervision over licensed affiliates and company employees to ensure violations of the chapter do not occur; failure to exercise adequate supervision is itself expressly made a violation of the chapter.

question: Under KRS 324.312, if a principal broker fails to return a terminated associate's license to the Commission within five business days of the request or termination, what is the consequence?
choice_a: The commission shall consider the license released, and the principal broker shall be in violation of KRS 324.160(4)(u)
choice_b: The associate's license is automatically revoked for five years
choice_c: The principal broker's E&O insurance is automatically canceled
choice_d: Nothing; the five-day period is only a non-binding guideline
explanation: KRS 324.312(2) provides that if a principal broker fails to return a license within five (5) business days as required, the commission shall consider the license released and the principal broker shall be in violation of KRS 324.160(4)(u) (improper, fraudulent, or dishonest dealing).

question: Under KRS 324.310(1), when a sales associate is discharged or terminates his or her association with the principal broker, what must the broker do?
choice_a: Wait 30 days to see whether the associate re-affiliates before taking any action
choice_b: Immediately deliver or mail the associate's license to the Commission along with a signed release statement, and notify the associate's last known address that this was done
choice_c: Destroy the associate's license certificate
choice_d: File a formal disciplinary complaint against the associate with the Commission
explanation: KRS 324.310(1) requires the broker to immediately deliver or mail the sales associate's license to the commission along with a release statement signed by the principal broker, and to notify the associate at his or her last known residence address that this was done.

question: Per KRS 324.010(11), a "designated manager" is defined as:
choice_a: Any unlicensed clerical employee who answers phones at a branch office
choice_b: The Commission's assigned regional field inspector
choice_c: A licensed sales associate or broker who manages a main or branch office for the principal broker, at the principal broker's direction, with managing authority over the sales associates at that office
choice_d: A broker who has personally managed at least five branch offices
explanation: KRS 324.010(11) defines a "designated manager" as a licensed sales associate or broker who manages a main or branch office for the principal broker, at the principal broker's direction, and has managing authority over the activities of the sales associates at that office.

question: KRS 324.010(15) defines "affiliation" as:
choice_a: A licensee's membership in a local Realtor association
choice_b: A referral partnership between two unrelated brokerage firms
choice_c: The act of co-listing a single property between two firms
choice_d: The relationship agreed upon between a licensee and a principal broker, and reported to the Commission, whereby the licensee places his or her license with the principal broker for supervision of the licensee's real estate brokerage activity
explanation: KRS 324.010(15) defines "affiliation" as the relationship agreed upon between a licensee and a principal broker and reported to the commission, where the licensee places his or her license with the principal broker for supervision of the licensee's real estate brokerage activity.

question: Under KRS 324.040(2), every applicant for a broker's or sales associate's license must state, among other things:
choice_a: The name of the person or company with which the applicant will be associated in the real estate business, and the location of the place for which the license is desired
choice_b: The applicant's projected first-year commission income
choice_c: The exact square footage of the applicant's intended office space
choice_d: The applicant's personal credit score
explanation: KRS 324.040(2) requires the applicant to state the name of the person or company with which he or she will be associated in the business of real estate and the location of the place for which the license is desired.
